<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    We consider the complex and symplectic elliptic Ginibre matrices of size
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:tex-math>$$(c+1)N \times (c+1)N$$</jats:tex-math>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mi>c</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mn>1</mml:mn>
                            <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mo>×</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mi>c</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mn>1</mml:mn>
                            <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , conditioned to have a deterministic eigenvalue at
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:tex-math>$$ p \in \mathbb {R} $$</jats:tex-math>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mi>p</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mo>∈</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mi>R</mml:mi>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    with multiplicity
                    <jats:italic>cN</jats:italic>
                    . We show that their limiting spectrum is either simply connected, doubly connected, or composed of two disjoint simply connected components. Moreover, denoting by
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:tex-math>$$\tau \in [0,1]$$</jats:tex-math>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mi>τ</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mo>∈</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mo>[</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mn>0</mml:mn>
                            <mml:mo>,</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mn>1</mml:mn>
                            <mml:mo>]</mml:mo>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    the non-Hermiticity parameter, we explicitly characterise the regions in the parameter space
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:tex-math>$$ (p, c, \tau ) $$</jats:tex-math>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mi>p</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mo>,</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mi>c</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mo>,</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mi>τ</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    where each topological type emerges. For cases where the droplet is either simply or doubly connected, we provide an explicit description of the limiting spectrum and the corresponding electrostatic energies. As an application, we derive the asymptotic behaviour of the moments of the characteristic polynomial for elliptic Ginibre matrices in the exponentially varying regime.
                  </jats:p>
title: Three Topological Phases of the Elliptic Ginibre Ensembles with a Point Charge

items.abstract: <jats:p>Continuous local polynomial splines are widely used in approximations, as well as in solving differential and integral equations.. In this paper, we consider the construction of continuously differentiable splines of the second-order of approximation. We construct continuously differentiable polynomial and non-polynomial splines by smoothing continuous local approximations. The construction of smoothed non-polynomial approximations is discussed using the example of constructing smooth trigonometric splines. Theoretical results are given. Results with numerical experiments are presented. Among the numerical experiments, the approximation on a non-uniform grid of nodes is considered, as well as the influence of introducing additional errors into the values of the function given at the grid nodes.</jats:p>
title: Smooth Polynomial and Non-polynomial Splines of the Second Order of Approximation

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We consider the elliptic Ginibre ensembles in the real, complex and symplectic symmetry classes. As the matrix size tends to infinity, we derive the asymptotic behaviour of the upper tail large deviation probabilities for both the spectral radius and the rightmost eigenvalue. More generally, we obtain asymptotic formulas for the probability that an eigenvalue is found in a prescribed region outside the support of the elliptic law, thereby providing a unified framework in which the results for the spectral radius and the rightmost eigenvalue appear as special cases. The key ingredient of our analysis is the precise asymptotic behaviour of the associated one-point functions, which is of independent interest.</jats:p>
title: Upper tail large deviations for extremal eigenvalues of the real, complex and symplectic elliptic Ginibre matrices

items.abstract: <jats:p>In this paper, we combine the notions of polynomial contractions [3], path-averaged contractions which appeared in [5] for metric spaces, in [6, 7] for b-metric spaces, in [8] in suprametric spaces, while their combined notion appeared in [9], and almost contractions [2], to introduce almost path-averaged polynomial contractions. We obtain a fixed point theorem for such contractions in the setting of metric spaces. Finally, we give an example showing that almost path-averaged polynomial contractions are not Banach contractions.</jats:p>
title: Almost Path-Averaged Polynomial Contractions: A New Generalization of Almost Polynomial Contractions, Almost Contractions, and Almost Path-Averaged Contractions

items.abstract: <jats:p>In the present paper, we generalize the result obtained in an earlier paper by the author with respect to recovering the singularity curves of a piecewise constant function of two variables by its Fourier-Jacobi coefficients. The method is based on a modified Prony’s method suggested in an earlier paper by us for recovering (approximating) the locations of discontinuities of a piecewise constant (smooth) function of one variable. It is shown that if the singularity curves of a piecewise polynomial function of two variables are polynomials and some indices of the Jacobi system are integers, then the curves can be approximated within&nbsp;$O(n^{−2})$ precision and the associated jump magnitudes within&nbsp;$O(n^{−1})$, given&nbsp;$O(n)$ Fourier-Jacobi coefficients of the function. For some nonconstant piecewise polynomial functions the singularity curves and the associated jump magnitudes may be recovered&nbsp;exactly. In addition, numerical examples are presented to illustrate the accuracy of the method.</jats:p>
title: Approximation of Polynomial Singularity Curves of Piecewise Polynomial Functions of Two Variables by Their Fourier-Jacobi Coefficients

items.abstract: We introduce a geometric framework for representing quantum entanglementthrough reduced entanglement coordinates derived from the Schmidt decompo-sition. For pure two-qubit states, the framework yields an entanglement conein which separability corresponds to geometric collapse to the cone apex. Thisconstruction extends naturally to higher-rank bipartitions through Schmidt-simplex geometries associated with Schmidt-rank reduction. For multipartitesystems, we introduce entanglement-graph coordinates that use pairwise bipar-tite reductions as geometric probes of global quantum states. The resultingrepresentation defines a local-unitary-invariant reduced geometry whose dimen-sion scales quadratically with subsystem number, compared with the exponentialscaling of the underlying pure-state space. Although not a complete invariantof multipartite entanglement, the graph geometry preserves important rela-tional and connectivity structure while remaining computationally tractable.Building on this representation, we develop a geometric interpretation of vari-ational quantum dynamics in which optimization trajectories evolve throughstructured regions of entanglement-graph space. We introduce Hamiltonian-selected entanglement-graph sectors, establish exact and perturbative sectorconstructions, derive local graph-distance energy relations near nondegenerateoptima, and develop learned geometric diagnostics for variational optimization.Numerical experiments on molecular and spin-chain Hamiltonians support thehypothesis that low-energy states concentrate near Hamiltonian-dependent graphsectors and demonstrate predictive information in the resulting geometric rep-resentations. Together, these results provide a unified geometric framework foranalyzing entanglement structure, quantum dynamics, and variational quantumoptimization.
title: Polynomial Geometric Reduction of Quantum Entanglement Dynamics

items.abstract: <jats:p>Modin and Verdier observed favorable long-time energy behavior for nonholonomic leapfrog in a rotating constrained-spring example that their reversibility argument did not explain. We investigate a foundational question: which polynomial conservation laws follow from the reflected update independently of the driver? For planar rank-one constraints and 0 &lt; h &lt; 2, we prove that the modified quadratic energy generates all common polynomial invariants, except at h = \( \sqrt{2} \), where an independent quartic generator appears. At this step, a change of variables turns the update into an exchange of squared lengths. This mechanism extends to arbitrary orthogonal-projector sequences in any dimension. The classification identifies the conservation shared by the update family; the original passenger-energy observation remains a separate question.</jats:p>
title: Universal Polynomial Invariants of Nonholonomic Leapfrog

items.abstract: The M\"{u}ntz polynomials are linear combinations of the system $\{x^{\lambda_0},x^{\lambda_1},\cdots, x^{\lambda_n}, \cdots\}$ associated to a complex sequence $\Lambda=\{\lambda_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2},\cdots\}$, which is a large extension of the classical polynomials. In this paper, we explore the basic approximation properties of M\"{u}ntz polynomials empirical interpolation method and its applicability for numerically integrating certain types of singular functions and solving differential equations having singular solutions.In particular, we capitalize on the generated basis functions and interpolation points to introduce a new type of quadrature formula suitable for M\"{u}ntz polynomials. Through numerical experiments, we examine the approximation properties of integrals involving functions having singularities at the boundaries of one-dimensional or two-dimensional non-tensor domains. By presenting numerical solutions of some singular differential problems, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed interpolation method and highlight its potential to compute high accurate solutions.
title: Empirical interpolation method for Muntz polynomial approximation
